title: 705. Queen Victoria’s Revenge: The Mad Emperor of Abyssinia (Part 1)

sentences.en: At Suez, one of our navy sloops will take you down the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 在苏伊士，我们的一艘海军单桅帆船会带你沿红海而下。

sentences.en: They'll have you at Zola, that's the port for Abyssinia, by the middle of February.
sentences.zh: 到二月中旬，他们会把你送到佐拉，那是去阿比西尼亚的港口。

sentences.en: And it can't take above a week to get the silver upcountry to this place called Attegrat.
sentences.zh: 把白银运到内陆一个叫阿特雷加特的地方，花不了过一个星期。

sentences.en: That's where General Napier will be.
sentences.zh: 内皮尔将军就在那里。

sentences.en: Napier?
sentences.zh: 内皮尔？

sentences.en: Not Bob the Bug Hunter.
sentences.zh: 不是那个打虫子的鲍勃吧。

sentences.en: What the blazes is he doing in Abyssinia?
sentences.zh: 他到底在阿比西尼亚鬼混什么？

sentences.en: We haven't got a station there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那儿又没有驻地。

sentences.en: Ah, we have by now, you may be sure.
sentences.zh: 啊，现在有了，你大可放心。

sentences.en: He was laughing in disbelief.
sentences.zh: 他难以置信地笑了起来。

sentences.en: You mean to tell me you haven't heard?
sentences.zh: 你是说你还没听说？

sentences.en: Why, he's invaded the place!
sentences.zh: 怎么，他已经把那地方给侵占了！

sentences.en: With an army!
sentences.zh: 带着军队！

sentences.en: From Inja!
sentences.zh: 从印度来的！

sentences.en: The silver is to help fund his campaign, don't you see?
sentences.zh: 这白银是为了帮他筹措军费，你明白吗？

sentences.en: Good God, Flashy, where have you been?
sentences.zh: 天哪，弗莱西，你到底去哪儿了？

sentences.en: Hold up?
sentences.zh: 站住？

sentences.en: Hold up, can't you?
sentences.zh: 站住，你不会吗？

sentences.en: Why is he invading?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要入侵？

sentences.en: To rescue the captives!
sentences.zh: 为了营救人质！

sentences.en: Captives!
sentences.zh: 人质！

sentences.en: Our consul!
sentences.zh: 我们的领事！

sentences.en: Envoys!
sentences.zh: 特使！

sentences.en: Missionaries!
sentences.zh: 传教士！

sentences.en: They're held prisoner by this mad cannibal king!
sentences.zh: 他们被这个疯狂的食人国王当成囚犯关押着！

sentences.en: And he's chaining them and flogging them and kicking up no end of a row!
sentences.zh: 而且他还用铁链锁他们、鞭打他们，闹得天翻地覆！

sentences.en: Teodros his name is!
sentences.zh: 他叫特奥多罗斯！

sentences.en: And you mean to say, you've not heard of him?
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，你没听说过他？

sentences.en: I'll be damned!
sentences.zh: 真见鬼！

sentences.en: Why, there's been uproar in Parliament!
sentences.zh: 怎么，议会里早就吵翻天了！

sentences.en: Our gracious Queen writing letters!
sentences.zh: 我们仁慈的女王都亲自写信了！

sentences.en: A penny or more on the income tax!
sentences.zh: 所得税都涨了至少一便士！

sentences.en: It's true!
sentences.zh: 千真万确！

sentences.en: So that is from a memoir by one of Victorian Britain's most decorated officers, General Sir Harry Flashman V.C., recalling his part in what he, in his memoir,
sentences.zh: 这段话摘自维多利亚时代英国功勋卓著的军官之一——哈里·弗莱西曼爵士（V.C.）的回忆录，他在书中回忆了自己参与的那场战争——

sentences.en: calls the strangest campaign in the history of British arMs.
sentences.zh: 他称之为英国军事史上最奇怪的战役。

sentences.en: And this is the subject of today's episode and our next episode, the Abyssinian Expedition of 1868.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们今天这期节目以及下一期节目的主题，1868年的阿比西尼亚远征。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that this isn't an expedition that is particularly well known.
sentences.zh: 我想可以公正地说，这并不是一次特别为人所知的远征。

sentences.en: So not one of the kind of the classic Victorian expeditions, but it is a banger.
sentences.zh: 所以它不算那种经典的维多利亚时期远征，但它绝对是个狠角色。

sentences.en: And if you go to pretty much any of Britain's leading museums, so the British Museum, the British Library, the V&A, the Bodleian,
sentences.zh: 如果你去英国几乎任何一家主要博物馆，比如大英博物馆、大英图书馆、维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆、博德利图书馆，

sentences.en: you will find manuscripts or relics or jewels or treasures that were brought back to Britain from this expedition.
sentences.zh: 你都会发现手稿、遗物、珠宝或宝藏，这些都是从这次远征中带回英国的。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we get complaints sometimes, don't we, from Canadian listeners that we don't have enough mentions of Canada on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们有时会接到加拿大听众的抱怨，对吧，说我们在播客里提到加拿大的次数不够多。

sentences.en: But I gather that some of this loot even found its way to the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 但我听说这些战利品中甚至有一些流落到了多伦多的安大略皇家博物馆。

sentences.en: So that's a lovely little nod to our Canadian listener, Mark Carney there, because I know he's a big fan of the rest of his history and he will enjoy that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我们的加拿大听众马克·卡尼来说是一个可爱的小致意，因为我知道他是我们节目的超级粉丝，他会喜欢那一刻的。

sentences.en: So yeah, those are treasures carried off by British troops after they stormed the mountain citadel of Magdala to rescue almost 60 European hostages this emperor,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这些都是英国军队在突袭马格达拉的山地城堡后运走的宝藏，当时皇帝——

sentences.en: Theodore Tuodros II, was holding.
sentences.zh: 特奥多罗斯二世（Tewodros II）正扣押着近60名人质。

sentences.en: And as you say, it's not a terribly well known Victorian escapade, but it is surely the maddeSt.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这不是一次广为人知的维多利亚时期的冒险，但它绝对是最疯狂的一次。

sentences.en: So in Sahari Flashman's memoirs, he recalls, and I quote, the screaming charge of long-haired warriors swinging their hideous sickle blades against the Sikh bayonets,
sentences.zh: 所以在哈里·弗莱西曼的回忆录中，他回忆道（我引用）："长发勇士们挥舞着可怕的镰刀状刀刃，伴随着尖叫冲向锡克教徒的刺刀，

sentences.en: the huge mound of rotting corpses under the precipice at Islamji, the ghastly forest of crucifixes at Gondar.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰吉悬崖下堆积如山的腐烂尸体，贡德尔令人毛骨悚然的十字架森林。"

sentences.en: Who doesn't love a ghastly forest of crucifixes?
sentences.zh: 谁不喜欢阴森恐怖的十字架森林呢？

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，一点没错。

sentences.en: Above all, he recalls, and I quote, the transformation of an urbane, cultivated monarch into a murderous tyrant,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他回忆道（我引用）："一个温文尔雅、饱学之士的君主变成了一个嗜杀成性的暴君，

sentences.en: shrieking with hysterical glee as he slashed and hacked at his bound victiMs.
sentences.zh: 他一边疯狂地狂笑，一边挥舞着砍向被绑受害者。"

sentences.en: I mean, I don't want to rain on the parade, but obviously this is from a novel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是故意泼冷水，但显然这是出自一部小说。

sentences.en: Flashman isn't real.
sentences.zh: 弗莱西曼并不是真人。

sentences.en: He's an invented character by George MacDonald Fraser for the avoidance of any doubt.
sentences.zh: 为了消除任何疑虑，他是乔治·麦克唐纳·弗雷泽虚构的人物。

sentences.en: But how much of this is exaggerated?
sentences.zh: 但其中有多少是被夸大的？

sentences.en: How much is true, do we think?
sentences.zh: 我们认为有多少是真的？

sentences.en: A little bit of it is exaggerated, but there's an awful lot of truth in this.
sentences.zh: 其中有一小部分被夸大了，但这里面有极其大量的真实成分。

sentences.en: So among the war correspondents who were embedded with the British troops, the British expedition that went to Magdala, one was Henry Morton Stanley,
sentences.zh: 因此，在随英军（前往马格达拉的英国远征军）深入敌后的战地记者中，其中一位是亨利·莫顿·斯坦利，

sentences.en: and another was the future imperial novelist G.A.
sentences.zh: 另一位是未来的帝国小说家G·A·

sentences.en: Henty.
sentences.zh: 亨蒂。

sentences.en: And Henty said this was an expedition to rank alongside the adventures of Hernán Cortés and Francisco Pizarro, which we've done on the show.
sentences.zh: 亨蒂曾说，这是一场可以与埃尔南·科尔特斯和弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗的冒险相提并论的远征，我们在节目中讲过他们。

sentences.en: And he's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 他没说错。

sentences.en: Do you think this inspired him in his novels?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这给了他小说的灵感吗？

sentences.en: Because as I remember, I read some of them.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得，我读过其中的一些。

sentences.en: They were always kind of with Clive to Calcutta, with Hannibal across the Alps, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 它们总是那种《跟随克莱夫去加尔各答》、《随汉尼拔翻越阿尔卑斯山》之类的内容。

sentences.en: And it always involved a journey.
sentences.zh: 而且总是涉及一段旅程。

sentences.en: Yes, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: Like King Solomon's Mines or something.
sentences.zh: 就像《所罗门王的宝藏》之类的。

sentences.en: The late Victorians and Edwardians, they love a journey.
sentences.zh: 晚期维多利亚时代的人和爱德华时代的人，他们太喜欢旅行了。

sentences.en: They love a quest and an expedition.
sentences.zh: 他们热爱寻求和远征。

sentences.en: And I think the fact that Henty had been on this incredible, you know, this incredible odyssey into the highlands of Abyssinia from the Red Sea coast,
sentences.zh: 我认为亨蒂曾有过这段不可思议的经历，你知道，深入阿比西尼亚高原、从红海海岸出发的这段不可思议的奥德赛之旅，

sentences.en: undoubtedly informed his writing.
sentences.zh: 无疑为他的写作提供了素材。

sentences.en: And there is something there's something terribly tragic about this story, but something really thrilling about it as well.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里有一种极其悲惨的成分，但也有一种非常扣人心弦的东西。

sentences.en: And Abyssinia is Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 阿比西尼亚就是埃塞俄比亚。

sentences.en: And Ethiopia, famously, is the country in Africa that was never colonized.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，埃塞俄比亚是非洲唯一没有被殖民的国家。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: But interesting that the British do get there even so.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，英国人即便如此还是去了那里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, and Tom, you will know this better than anybody.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这件事你比任何人都清楚。

sentences.en: Well, anybody outside Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 好吧，埃塞俄比亚以外的任何人。

sentences.en: It's also the second oldest Christian country in the world, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 它也是世界上第二古老的基督教国家，不是吗？

sentences.en: After Armenia.
sentences.zh: 仅次于亚美尼亚。

sentences.en: So, I think it embraced Christianity in 330 AD.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想它在公元330年就皈依了基督教。

sentences.en: Though, when Band-Aid asked, do they know it's Christmas?
sentences.zh: 虽然当Band-Aid问“他们知道今天是圣诞节吗”时，

sentences.en: Yeah, they absolutely know it's Christmas.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们绝对知道今天是圣诞节。

sentences.en: They absolutely did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们当然知道，是的。

sentences.en: They have done for much longer than we have.
sentences.zh: 他们比我们知道的时间要早得多。

sentences.en: But after that, just to give people a sense.
sentences.zh: 但在此之后，只是为了让人们有个概念。

sentences.en: So, Abyssinia, as it was called in the 19th century, it became effectively cut off from sort of the Mediterranean and the world that became Christendom.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如19世纪所称的阿比西尼亚，它实际上与地中海以及成为基督教世界的那个世界隔绝了。

sentences.en: And so, it became shrouded in mystery.
sentences.zh: 因此，它被笼罩在神秘之中。

sentences.en: And people in sort of medieval Europe used to love the idea of Presta John, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 中世纪欧洲的人们过去常常喜欢约翰长老的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: This kind of lost Christian king who might be in India or he might be somewhere in Africa.
sentences.zh: 这种失落的基督教君主可能在印度，也可能在非洲的某个地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, people have often wondered whether this was some sort of buried ancestral memory of this lost Christian realm of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们经常想知道这是否是关于阿比西尼亚这个失落的基督教王国的某种埋藏在祖先记忆深处的东西。

sentences.en: Anyway, in the 1520s, the Portuguese turned up.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，在1520年代，葡萄牙人出现了。

sentences.en: It's always the Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 总是葡萄牙人。

sentences.en: And then, for the next few centuries, very slowly, the outside world intrudes on this kind of mountain kingdom.
sentences.zh: 然后，在接下来的几个世纪里，外部世界非常缓慢地闯入了这个山地王国。

sentences.en: So, you have the Ottomans who were on the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有在红海的奥斯曼人。

sentences.en: And then, the early 19th century, the Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 然后，在19世纪初，埃及人来了。

sentences.en: So, the Egyptians are sort of pushing up the Nile through Sudan.
sentences.zh: 所以埃及人正通过苏丹沿着尼罗河向上推进。

sentences.en: And both of these powers are Muslim.
sentences.zh: 这两大势力都是穆斯林的。

sentences.en: And Ethiopia, obviously, is Christian.
sentences.zh: 而埃塞俄比亚显然是基督教的。

sentences.en: So, that's adding a further dimension of tension.
sentences.zh: 所以，这增添了又一层紧张关系。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, there's a strain of nativism that runs through this story, I think, of nationalism, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这个故事贯穿着一种本土主义的暗流，我想还有民族主义。

sentences.en: And a fear of encirclement by Muslim powers.
sentences.zh: 以及对被穆斯林势力包围的恐惧。

sentences.en: And a fear that other Christians, heretical Christians, will sell them out.
sentences.zh: 以及担心其他基督徒、异端基督徒会出卖他们。

sentences.en: Well, we did an episode on the Ark of the Covenant, which Ethiopia claims to have.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一期关于约柜的节目，埃塞俄比亚声称自己拥有约柜。

sentences.en: And the Ethiopian royal family claimed descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚王室声称自己是所罗门和示巴女王的后代。

sentences.en: So, they have, you know, they have very, very deep links to the kind of the mythology of the Bible in a way that no other Christian kingdom does.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们与圣经神话有着非常非常深厚的联系，这是其他任何基督教王国所没有的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they feel, well, they feel they own the story.
sentences.zh: 而且他们觉得，嗯，他们觉得他们拥有这个故事。

sentences.en: And other people are newcomers and parvenues and so on.
sentences.zh: 其他人都是新来者和暴发户等等。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's kick off in 1843.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，让我们从1843年开始。

sentences.en: So, 1843, this young British visitor arrives in Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 所以在1843年，这位年轻的英国访客抵达了阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: And his name is Walter Plowden.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫沃尔特·普劳登。

sentences.en: And he's 23 years old.
sentences.zh: 他今年23岁。

sentences.en: Plowden was born in India to a civil service family.
sentences.zh: 普劳登出生于印度的公务员家庭。

sentences.en: But he's a kind of restless, adventurous sort of young man.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个不安分、喜欢冒险的年轻人。

sentences.en: He's eager to see action.
sentences.zh: 他渴望看到行动。

sentences.en: And he was going back to England when he stopped in Suez.
sentences.zh: 他在苏伊士停留，正准备回英格兰。

sentences.en: And he met a Scottish sailor called John Bell.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了一位名叫约翰·贝尔的苏格兰水手。

sentences.en: And John Bell said to him, you know, I've always had this dream of going to look for the source of the White Nile.
sentences.zh: 约翰·贝尔对他说，你知道，我一直有个梦想，去寻找白尼罗河的源头。

sentences.en: And Plowden said, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 普劳登说，太棒了。

sentences.en: Why don't we do it?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不一起去呢？

sentences.en: I'll come along.
sentences.zh: 算我一个。

sentences.en: Yeah, because that's a peak Victorian activity.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为那是巅峰的维多利亚时期活动。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, they set off.
sentences.zh: 于是他们出发了。

sentences.en: They went south.
sentences.zh: 他们向南走。

sentences.en: They went into the mountains of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 他们走进了阿比西尼亚的山脉。

sentences.en: And they absolutely loved it.
sentences.zh: 他们简直太喜欢那里了。

sentences.en: And this guy Plowden, he wrote about it afterwards.
sentences.zh: 这个叫普劳登的家伙后来写下了这段经历。

sentences.en: He said, it's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他说，这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: It's basically like going back in time to the high Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 基本上就像时光倒流回了盛期中世纪。

sentences.en: It's warlords.
sentences.zh: 这里有军阀。

sentences.en: It's feasts.
sentences.zh: 有盛宴。

sentences.en: It's battles.
sentences.zh: 有战斗。

sentences.en: It's chivalry.
sentences.zh: 有骑士精神。

sentences.en: He says, you know, life in Britain and in Western Europe now is very boring and industrial and suburban.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，现在英国和西欧的生活非常无聊、工业化且充满市侩气。

sentences.en: But this is fantastic.
sentences.zh: 但这太棒了。

sentences.en: There is no parallel to it, he said, in this steaming and telegraphing world.
sentences.zh: 他说，在这个充满蒸汽和电报的世界里，根本找不到与之相比的东西。

sentences.en: Well, the steam and the steamship and the telegraph and the railway are things we'll be talking about in a little while.
sentences.zh: 嗯，蒸汽、轮船、电报和铁路是我们一会儿要谈的事情。

sentences.en: So, they went into Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 所以他们走进了阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: Bell married an Abyssinian woman and became a kind of military officer in Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 贝尔娶了一个阿比西尼亚女人，并在阿比西尼亚成为了一名类似军官的人物。

sentences.en: And Plowden had all kinds of mad adventures and escapades and captures and escapes.
sentences.zh: 普劳登经历了各种疯狂的冒险、奇遇、被捕和逃脱。

sentences.en: And eventually, he decided to go back to England.
sentences.zh: 最终，他决定回英格兰。

sentences.en: Inevitably, he was shipwrecked in the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，他的船在红海失事了。

sentences.en: But finally, he got back.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他回去了。

sentences.en: And in 1848, he was appointed by the Foreign Office as Britain's first consul at a place called Massawa, which is a Red Sea port.
sentences.zh: 1848年，他被外交部任命为英国驻马萨瓦（一个红海港口）的第一任领事。

sentences.en: It's now in Eritrea, and Massawa was basically the gateway from the sea into this landlocked kingdom of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 它现在属于厄立特里亚，而马萨瓦基本上是从海洋通往阿比西尼亚这个内陆王国的门户。

sentences.en: And Plowden's great dream, he's a huge, I don't know if this is a word, Abyssinia-phile.
sentences.zh: 普劳den的伟大梦想是——他是一个狂热的（我不知道这算不算一个词）“阿比西尼亚迷”。

sentences.en: And his dream is to arrange a permanent treaty that will cement Anglo-Abyssinian friendship.
sentences.zh: 他的梦想是促成一项永久条约，以巩固英阿友谊。

sentences.en: The problem is that Abyssinia is very turbulent.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，阿比西尼亚非常动荡。

sentences.en: It's basically locked into this permanent Wars of the Roses.
sentences.zh: 它基本上陷入了一种永无止境的“玫瑰战争”状态。

sentences.en: So, you already mentioned there's an ancient dynasty that is descended from Solomon, and therefore from David.
sentences.zh: 所以，你刚才提到这里有一个古老的王朝，据称是所罗门的后代，因此也是大卫的后代。

sentences.en: But they have basically become powerless.
sentences.zh: 但他们基本上已经失去了实权。

sentences.en: And there's huge infighting between warlords and pretenders and kingmakers and different kind of provincial strongmen and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 军阀、觊觎王位者、拥立国王者、各种地方强人等等之间发生了巨大的内斗。

sentences.en: Impossible to follow.
sentences.zh: 根本理不清头绪。

sentences.en: And perhaps as a result, as a reaction to this instability, there is a tradition in Abyssinia by the 19th century
sentences.zh: 也许正因如此，作为对这种不稳定局面的反应，到了19世纪，阿比西尼亚流传着一种传统

sentences.en: that a Messiah, descended from Solomon and David, will one day arise, he will crush all his rivals,
sentences.zh: 即一位源自所罗门和大卫血统的弥赛亚终有一天会崛起，他将粉碎所有对手，

sentences.en: he will unite this fractured country, he will wipe the floor with their enemies, the Egyptians,
sentences.zh: 他将统一这个分裂的国家，把他们的敌人埃及人打得落花流水，

sentences.en: and he will march all the way to Jerusalem to restore the true faith in the holy city.
sentences.zh: 他将一路进军耶路撒冷，在圣城恢复真正的信仰。

sentences.en: And tradition has it that his name will be Theodros, Theodore, the gift of God.
sentences.zh: 传统记载他的名字叫Theodros，也就是西奥多，意为“上帝的恩赐”。

sentences.en: And there are occasionally kind of false Theodors, false Theodroses, but none of them kind of stick.
sentences.zh: 偶尔也会出现一些假冒的西奥多，但没有一个能成气候。

sentences.en: And then, in March 1855, Plowden sends a message to the Foreign Office in London.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1855年3月，普劳den向伦敦外交部发去了消息。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: There is at last some chance that Abyssinia may be united under one sovereign, and such a one as shall merit the support and friendship of Her Majesty's Government.
sentences.zh: “阿比西尼亚终于有了一些在一位君主统治下实现统一的可能，而这位君主值得女王陛下的政府予以支持和友谊。”

sentences.en: And the bloke he's talking about is a man called Kassa, who's from the north of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 他所说的那个人名叫卡萨，来自阿比西尼亚北部。

sentences.en: And what we know of this guy Kassa, he was born in 1818 or thereabouts, so he's probably in his mid-30s at this point.
sentences.zh: 关于这个叫卡萨的人，我们所了解的是他出生于1818年前后，所以此时他大概三十多岁。

sentences.en: He has an obscure background.
sentences.zh: 他的出身默默无闻。

sentences.en: He seems to have been educated in a monastery, which was attacked by bandits, and then he escaped.
sentences.zh: 他似乎曾在一家修道院受过教育，后来该修道院遭到土匪袭击，他逃了出来。

sentences.en: He became an outlaw himself, a kind of bandit leader.
sentences.zh: 他自己也成了一个法外之徒，某种意义上的匪首。

sentences.en: But no hint, no hint that he's descended from a biblical king.
sentences.zh: 但没有任何迹象表明他是某个圣经国王的后代。

sentences.en: No, at this point, no hint that he's descended from Solomon.
sentences.zh: 不，此时没有任何迹象表明他是所罗门的后代。

sentences.en: Although, of course, he will claim descent from Solomon later.
sentences.zh: 尽管当然，他后来会声称自己是所罗门的后代。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So Kassa is a sort of bold, courageous, charismatic man.
sentences.zh: 所以卡萨是一个大胆、勇敢且极具个人魅力的男人。

sentences.en: He's obviously a good leader of men.
sentences.zh: 他显然是个出色的领袖。

sentences.en: He beats one rival after another in the 1840s, early 1850s.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪40年代和50年代初，他一个接一个地击败了竞争对手。

sentences.en: Then in January 1855, he beats his last major rival, and he assembles all his troops, and he says,
sentences.zh: 接着在1855年1月，他击败了最后一个主要对手，集结了所有军队，并说道：

sentences.en: I've won.
sentences.zh: “我赢了。”

sentences.en: I'm the new emperor of Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: “我是阿比西尼亚的新皇帝。”

sentences.en: And to mark the occasion, I am taking a new name, and that name is Theodros.
sentences.zh: “为了庆祝这一刻，我将起用一个新名字，这个名字就是西奥多（Theodros）。”

sentences.en: So he is Theodros II, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他是西奥多二世，对吧？

sentences.en: And I was thinking, well, who was Theodros I?
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，那西奥多一世是谁呢？

sentences.en: So I did some detailed research in the Bodleman.
sentences.zh: 于是在博德利图书馆里，我做了一些详细的研究。

sentences.en: In the Bodleman Library?
sentences.zh: 在博德利图书馆？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's kind of King Arthur figure, who reigned around the same time that Henry V was winning the Battle of Agincourt, for about nine months.
sentences.zh: 他有点像亚瑟王式的人物，在位大约九个月，其统治时期大致与亨利五世赢得阿金库尔战役的时期相当。

sentences.en: And James Bruce, an explorer in the 19th century, said, there must have been something very brilliant that happened under this prince, but no one can remember what it is.
sentences.zh: 19世纪的探险家詹姆斯·布鲁斯曾说过：“这位君主统治时期必定发生过非常辉煌的事情，但已经没人记得是什么了。”

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So anyway, this guy, Kasser, now Theodros, is the protagonist of our story.
sentences.zh: 总之，这家伙卡萨，也就是现在的西奥多，是我们故事的主角。

sentences.en: Flashman, you may recall, called him a murderous tyrant shrieking with hysterical glee.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，弗莱什曼称他为“一个发出歇斯底里狂喜尖叫的嗜血暴君”。

sentences.en: And Alan Moorhead, who wrote two brilliant books on the history of the Nile, said he has a reputation in the historiography of a mad dog let loose,
sentences.zh: 而写过两本关于尼罗河历史的杰出著作的阿兰·穆尔head则表示，他在史学界有着“放鞴狂犬”般的声誉，

sentences.en: a sort of black reincarnation of Ivan the Terrible.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上是伊凡雷帝的黑色转世。

sentences.en: But I think this is very unfair, because actually, when Ploughton first visited this guy's camp,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这非常不公平，因为实际上，当普劳den第一次访问这家伙的营地时——

sentences.en: Theodros liked to spend a lot of time on campaigns, so he was always in tents.
sentences.zh: 西奥多喜欢把大量时间花在行军打仗上，所以他总是住在帐篷里。

sentences.en: He visits his camp in summer 1855, and he's actually very impressed by Theodros.
sentences.zh: 他在1855年夏天访问了西奥多的营地，实际上对西奥多印象极深。

sentences.en: He finds him kind of reclining on a divan, surrounded by musicians playing flutes and banging druMs.
sentences.zh: 他发现西奥多斜靠在一张长椅上，周围环绕着吹笛子和敲鼓的音乐家。

sentences.en: So very kind of, this is absolute, you know, European meeting indigenous king bingo.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常符合……你知道的，这就是“欧洲人会见本土君主”的典型情景。

sentences.en: Yes, reclining on a divan is pretty much obligatory, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，斜靠在长椅上几乎是标配，对吧？

sentences.en: Obligatory, exactly.
sentences.zh: 标配，确实如此。

sentences.en: And actually, in his report to the Foreign Office, he said, this guy is very charming and very impressive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在给外交部的报告中说，这家伙非常迷人，给人留下了深刻的印象。

sentences.en: He's young, he's vigorous, he's polite and engaging when pleased, and mostly displaying great tact and delicacy.
sentences.zh: 他年轻、充满活力、高兴时彬彬有礼且引人入胜，绝大多数时候都表现出极大的机智和细腻。

sentences.en: He said, Theodros is very dedicated to the idea of restoring the glories of the Ethiopian Empire and achieving great conquests.
sentences.zh: 他说，西奥多非常致力于恢复埃塞俄比亚帝国昔日辉煌并取得伟大征服的理念。

sentences.en: He's a man of untiring energy, his personal and moral daring is boundless.
sentences.zh: 他是一个精力永不枯竭的人，其个人和道德上的胆识无边无际。

sentences.en: Now, there are a couple of flaws that Ploughton notes as well.
sentences.zh: 不过，普劳den也注意到了一些缺点。

sentences.en: His violent anger at times, his unyielding pride as regards his kingly and divine right, and his fanatical religious zeal.
sentences.zh: 他有时会勃然大怒，对自己的君王身份和神圣权力有着毫不妥协的傲慢，并且有着狂热的宗教热忱。

sentences.en: However, Ploughton says this is a man we can do business with.
sentences.zh: 然而，普劳den表示，这是一个我们可以合作的人。

sentences.en: He wants to reclaim Abyssinia's ancient borders.
sentences.zh: 他想要收复阿比西尼亚古老的边界。

sentences.en: He dreams of retaking Egypt for Christianity, marching all the way to Cairo and Alexandria, and then, and I quote, a triumphant march to the Holy Sepulchre.
sentences.zh: 他梦想着为基督教夺回埃及，一路进军开罗和亚历山大，然后——请允许我引用原话——“进行一次通往圣墓的凯旋进军”。

sentences.en: Can I ask, the Foreign Office in London wouldn't necessarily approve of these goals, would they?
sentences.zh: 请问，伦敦的外交部不一定会赞同这些目标吧？

sentences.en: I think they're mad goals.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是疯狂的目标。

sentences.en: Because this, of course, is the period when they're starting to think about the Suez Canal.
sentences.zh: 因为这当然是他们开始考虑苏伊士运河的时期。

sentences.en: They don't want to offend the Ottomans.
sentences.zh: 他们不想得罪奥斯曼人。

sentences.en: No, they don't want to offend the Ottomans, particularly with whom they, of course, they're allied in the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 对，他们不想得罪奥斯曼人，尤其是他们当然还在克里米亚战争中与奥斯曼人结盟。

sentences.en: I mean, British interests in Egypt are extremely important to them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，英国在埃及的利益对他们来说极为重要。

sentences.en: They do not want to alienate the Egyptians, and this, as we will see, becomes a problem.
sentences.zh: 他们不想疏远埃及人，正如我们接下来将看到的，这成了一个问题。

sentences.en: So on top of that, Britain is a Christian power.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，英国是一个基督教强国。

sentences.en: Ethiopia is a Christian power.
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚是一个基督教强国。

sentences.en: Is there any sense that, therefore, they are natural allies?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着他们天然就是盟友？

sentences.en: Or is Britain simply, it's all about real politics, it's all about imperial priorities, the Christian element just doesn't really enter the calculations of diplomats in London?
sentences.zh: 还是说英国完全出于现实政治，完全出于帝国利益的优先考虑，基督教元素根本不在伦敦外交官的考量之内？

sentences.en: It's important to some people.
sentences.zh: 这对某些人来说很重要。

sentences.en: It's definitely important to Ploughton.
sentences.zh: 对普劳den来说绝对重要。

sentences.en: It's important, as we will see, to lots of missionaries and missionary organizations.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将会看到的，这对许多传教士和传教组织也很重要。

sentences.en: But not to the government.
sentences.zh: 但对政府而言并非如此。

sentences.en: But to the government, I would argue, probably not.
sentences.zh: 但我可以说，对于政府来说，大概并非如此。

sentences.en: I think they certainly have religious prejudices, but there's an awful lot of realpolitik in this, as we will find out.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们肯定有宗教偏见，但正如我们将发现的那样，其中包含了极多的现实政治考量。

sentences.en: Anyway, Ploughton says to Theodros,
sentences.zh: 无论如何，普劳den对西奥多说：

sentences.en: would you like to sign a treaty with Britain?
sentences.zh: “你愿意与英国签署一项条约吗？”

sentences.en: And Theodros hesitates.
sentences.zh: 西奥多犹豫了。

sentences.en: What he doesn't want to do is sign a treaty that would give British agents in Abyssinia diplomatic immunity.
sentences.zh: 他最不想做的事情，就是签署一项给予英国在阿比西尼亚特工外交豁免权的条约。

sentences.en: He says, you know, my word is law, and anything that undermines our sovereignty, I'm not happy with.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我的一言九鼎，任何削弱我们主权的事情我都无法接受。

sentences.en: So I don't really want to sign a treaty with you, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以事实上，我其实并不想跟你签条约。

sentences.en: And Ploughton thinks, well, fine, maybe he'll come round in time.
sentences.zh: 普劳den觉得，好吧，也许假以时日他会想通的。

sentences.en: And actually, Theodros doesn't seem like a terrible investment.
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，西奥多看起来并不是一个糟糕的投资对象。

sentences.en: So Flashman paints him as this, you know, demonic, kind of drunken maniac.
sentences.zh: 所以弗莱什曼把他描绘成这样一个恶魔般、有些酒鬼般的狂人。

sentences.en: But there are lots of ways in which he's actually quite forward-thinking.
sentences.zh: 但在很多方面，他其实相当具有前瞻性思维。

sentences.en: He's a would-be modernizer, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他是一个潜在的现代主义者。

sentences.en: He wants to stamp out the power of the regional warlords.
sentences.zh: 他想要根除地方军阀的势力。

sentences.en: He wants to build a new road network.
sentences.zh: 他想要构建一个新的道路网络。

sentences.en: He wants a new system of royal justice.
sentences.zh: 他想要一套新的王室司法体系。

sentences.en: You could see him as a sort of Henry VII or something, you know, wanting to impose order after years of chaos.
sentences.zh: 你可以把他看作类似于亨利七世之类的人物，你知道的，希望在多年的混乱之后重建秩序。

sentences.en: He wants to fight slavery because, of course, the slave trade across the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean is controlled by his Muslim rivals.
sentences.zh: 他想要禁绝奴隶制，因为红海和印度洋的奴隶贸易当然是由他的穆斯林对手控制的。

sentences.en: And is that a kind of a gesture of economic warfare against the Ottomans?
sentences.zh: 这算是一种针对奥斯曼人的经济战姿态吗？

sentences.en: Or is there any humanitarian impulse there at all?
sentences.zh: 还是说其中完全带有任何出于人道主义的冲动？

sentences.en: That is a hard thing to say because all that we know of, we don't really have that much insight into his inner world.
sentences.zh: 这很难说，因为我们对他的内心世界其实并没有太多深入的了解。

sentences.en: I suspect there's an awful lot of kind of political expediency in it, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我怀疑其中包含了大量的政治权宜之计。

sentences.en: He also wants, for very Peter the Great-like, he wants to change the way people dress.
sentences.zh: 出于一种非常类似彼得大帝的动机，他还想改变人们的着装方式。

sentences.en: So he wants Abyssinians to wear proper clothes.
sentences.zh: 所以他希望阿比西尼亚人穿得体面。

sentences.en: He wants them to wear shirts with special coloured sleeves if they've done great service to the state.
sentences.zh: 他希望那些为国家立下大功的人穿带有特殊颜色袖子的衬衫。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 这倒挺不错的。

sentences.en: And he's absolutely fascinated by the outside world.
sentences.zh: 而且他对外部世界极为着迷。

sentences.en: So he loves meeting travellers.
sentences.zh: 所以他喜欢结识旅行者。

sentences.en: He loves hearing about Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢听闻有关英国和法国的事。

sentences.en: France, he's obsessed with the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 对于法国以及克里米亚战争，他简直着了迷。

sentences.en: So that's something that will be coming up in the rest of this history before the end of the year, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这将会是今年年底之前这部历史剩余部分中会涉及的内容，对吧？

sentences.en: We'll be doing a series about the Crimean War.
sentences.zh: 我们将做一个关于克里米亚战争的系列节目。

sentences.en: So Teodros would have loved that because when travellers come, he always sort of says, what news from Balaclava?
sentences.zh: 所以西奥多一定会喜欢这个，因为当旅行者到来时，他总是会问：“巴拉克拉瓦有什么新消息吗？”

sentences.en: Tell me of Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: “给我讲讲塞瓦斯托波尔的事。”

sentences.en: You know, he cannot wait to get all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他急切地想要了解所有这些事情。

sentences.en: Doesn't he end up having a gun called Sebastopol in due course?
sentences.zh: 他最终是不是顺理成章地拥有一门名叫“塞瓦斯托波尔”的大炮？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他的确有。

sentences.en: His favourite possession, a gun called Sebastopol.
sentences.zh: 他最喜爱的财产是一门名为塞瓦斯托波尔的大炮。

sentences.en: So it really has had an impact on him.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他确实产生了影响。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the Crimean War fascinates him and bewilders him.
sentences.zh: 但克里米亚战争既让他着迷，又让他感到困惑。

sentences.en: He cannot get his head around the fact that Christian Britain and France are allied with Muslim Turkey, the Ottoman Empire, against another Christian power, Russia.
sentences.zh: 他无法理解这样一个事实：基督教的英国和法国居然与穆斯林土耳其（奥斯曼帝国）结盟，去对抗另一个基督教强国俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He really struggles to comprehend that.
sentences.zh: 他实在难以理解这一点。

sentences.en: And that makes him wonder whether the British are quite as devoted to Christianity as they should be.
sentences.zh: 这让他怀疑英国人是否真的像他们应有的那样忠于基督教。

sentences.en: Anyway, a year later, end of 1856, he has the highest ranking visitor he will ever receive.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，一年后，即1856年底，他迎来了他将接待过的最高级别访客。

sentences.en: And this is the Coptic patriarch, Cyril IV, who is the sort of spiritual father of the Ethiopian church.
sentences.zh: 这就是科普特牧首西里尔四世，他可以说是埃塞俄比亚教会的精神之父。

sentences.en: And he comes to visit from Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 他从亚历山大前来访问。

sentences.en: And Cyril turns up and he is very, very down on Abyssinian religious practice.
sentences.zh: 西里尔一出现，就对阿比西尼亚的宗教习俗表现出非常非常不屑的态度。

sentences.en: Cyril says, look, you have far too many holidays, holy days.
sentences.zh: 西里尔说：“听着，你们的节日、圣日实在太多了。”

sentences.en: You have far too many saints and they're all wrong.
sentences.zh: “你们的圣人实在太多了，而且全都不对。”

sentences.en: Your calendar is bonkers, all of this.
sentences.zh: “你们的历法简直荒谬绝伦，诸如此类。”

sentences.en: And Teodros, he completely conforms to Plowden's picture of him because Plowden said he was very hot-tempered and proud.
sentences.zh: 而西奥多完全符合普劳den对他的描述，因为普劳den说过他脾气火爆且极其傲慢。

sentences.en: He goes ballistic at this.
sentences.zh: 听到这话，他彻底暴怒了。

sentences.en: He locks up the patriarch for a little while.
sentences.zh: 他把这位牧首关押了一小段时间。

sentences.en: And the rumors sweep Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 传言迅速席卷了整个阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: Well, Teodros has fallen under the sway of the English.
sentences.zh: “西里尔，西奥多已经落入了英国人的掌控之中。”

sentences.en: Maybe he's going to convert to Protestantism.
sentences.zh: “也许他要改信新教了。”

sentences.en: And he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有。

sentences.en: Eventually, he releases this patriarch and he kneels to ask his forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 最终，他释放了这位牧首，并下跪请求对方原谅。

sentences.en: And he says, I'm sorry, I locked you up.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我很抱歉把你关起来。”

sentences.en: And Cyril says, the problem of the year is you've been listening to English visitors.
sentences.zh: 而西里尔说：“这几年的问题在于你一直在听信英国访客的话。”

sentences.en: Don't trust the English.
sentences.zh: “不要相信英国人。”

sentences.en: They're only pretending to be your friends.
sentences.zh: “他们只是假装是你的朋友。”

sentences.en: They are plotting, and I quote, to undermine your power and conquer your country.
sentences.zh: “他们正在阴谋——请允许我引用原话——‘削弱你的力量并征服你的国家’。”

sentences.en: Which they're not, to be fair to the English.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，英国人并没有这么做。

sentences.en: No, which they're not.
sentences.zh: 不，他们确实没有。

sentences.en: Which they're absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对没有这么做。

sentences.en: But this is a thread that will run through this story.
sentences.zh: 但这是贯穿这个故事的一条线索。

sentences.en: I think because the Abyssinians have been so isolated for so long, they have got it into their heads that their neighbors are all plotting to sell them out
sentences.zh: 我想，由于阿比西尼亚人长期与世隔绝，他们的脑子里已经根深蒂固地认为他们的邻居都在密谋出卖他们

sentences.en: or undermine them or conquer them or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者削弱他们、征服他们诸如此类的。

sentences.en: I suppose, to be fair to him, I mean, the British do have a certain track record in.
sentences.zh: 我想，公平起见，英国人在某些方面确实有前科……

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们的确有。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, at this point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，至少在目前这个阶段是这样。

sentences.en: If you listen to the French, they do.
sentences.zh: 如果你听法国人的说法，他们的确这么认为。

sentences.en: But Teodros is actually still quite devoted to the British.
sentences.zh: 但特奥德罗斯其实仍然相当忠于英国人。

sentences.en: He still craves their approval.
sentences.zh: 他依然渴望得到他们的认可。

sentences.en: He recognizes that they're the most powerful, the richest, the most modern country on earth.
sentences.zh: 他承认他们是地球上最强大、最富有、最现代化的国家。

sentences.en: And so, when the patriarch leaves, he takes with him two letters.
sentences.zh: 因此，当长老离开时，他带走了两封信。

sentences.en: And one of them was dictated by Teodros himself.
sentences.zh: 其中一封是特奥德罗斯本人口授的。

sentences.en: And this was a letter dictated to Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 这是一封口授给维多利亚女王的信。

sentences.en: May this letter, sent by the King of Kings, Teodros of Ethiopia, reach the Queen of England,
sentences.zh: 愿这封由万王之王、埃塞俄比亚的特奥德罗斯所发出的信件，能送达英格兰女王，

sentences.en: Victoria.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Are you well?
sentences.zh: 你身体好吗？

sentences.en: I am well, thank God.
sentences.zh: 我很好，感谢上帝。

sentences.en: I have received your envoy with love and friendship.
sentences.zh: 我带着爱与友谊收到了你的使者。

sentences.en: Now you are the child of Christ, and I am the child of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 现在你是基督的孩子，而我是基督的孩子。

sentences.en: For the love of Christ, I want friendship.
sentences.zh: 为了基督的爱，我想要建立友谊。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 所以这挺好的。

sentences.en: That's a great letter.
sentences.zh: 这是一封很棒的信。

sentences.en: It's a fantastic letter.
sentences.zh: 这是一封了不起的信。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Are you well?
sentences.zh: 你身体好吗？

sentences.en: I'm well.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I think he's my favorite Abyssinian king.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是我最喜欢的阿比西尼亚国王。

sentences.en: It's basically like a cold call from a call center, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像呼叫中心打来的骚扰电话，对吧？

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: How's your day going?
sentences.zh: 你今天过得怎么样？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，才不是。

sentences.en: It's like a pen pal.
sentences.zh: 这就像是笔友通信。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's cool.
sentences.zh: 对，这很酷。

sentences.en: That's what it's like.
sentences.zh: 就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: So, the other letter is from Plowden to the Foreign Office.
sentences.zh: 所以，另一封信是普劳登写给外交部的。

sentences.en: And Plowden says, I think we should cement the relationship with Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 普劳登说，我认为我们应该巩固与阿比西尼亚的关系。

sentences.en: Could you please send Teodros some guns and ammunition and a handsome piece for his own use, like a hunting rifle?
sentences.zh: 你们能否请送给特奥德罗斯一些枪支弹药，以及一把供他个人使用的精美猎枪？

sentences.en: Well, this is in 1857, and two years go by, and Plowden and Teodros hear nothing back.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是在1857年，两年过去了，普劳登和特奥德罗斯什么回音也没收到。

sentences.en: And then, at last, Plowden gets a message from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后，终于，普劳登收到了来自海岸的消息。

sentences.en: London have sent him a package.
sentences.zh: 伦敦给他寄了一个包裹。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 里面是什么？

sentences.en: There's a rifle, a screwdriver, and a case.
sentences.zh: 里面有一把步枪、一把螺丝刀和一个盒子。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定。

sentences.en: It's unclear whether the case is for the rifle or the screwdriver.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚这个盒子是装步枪的还是装螺丝刀的。

sentences.en: It's for the screwdriver.
sentences.zh: 它是用来装螺丝刀的。

sentences.en: And that is it.
sentences.zh: 这就是全部了。

sentences.en: And his heart sinks, because he knows this won't go down well with Teodros.
sentences.zh: 他的心顿时凉了半截，因为他知道这在特奥德罗斯那里肯定讨不到好。

sentences.en: It's not even a letter.
sentences.zh: 这甚至都算不上一封信。

sentences.en: And the truth is, of course, the Foreign Office don't really care.
sentences.zh: 当然，事实是，外交部根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Abyssinia is like a massive backwater.
sentences.zh: 阿比西尼亚就像是一个极其偏远的死水潭。

sentences.en: No one really cares about it.
sentences.zh: 根本没人真正在乎它。

sentences.en: It's also, they've had the Indian mutiny raging, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 而且，他们当时还面临着印度民族大起义，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, they've had other things on their mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们有别的事要操心。

sentences.en: They've got other things on their mind.
sentences.zh: 他们有别的事情要操心。

sentences.en: Anyway, time goes by.
sentences.zh: 总之，时间流逝。

sentences.en: Teodros gets on with fighting the kind of regional warlords and trying to unite the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 特奥德罗斯继续与地方军阀作战，并试图统一王国。

sentences.en: But it's much bloodier and more grueling than he expected.
sentences.zh: 但这比他预期的要血腥和残酷得多。

sentences.en: He stamps out one rebellion.
sentences.zh: 他刚平息了一场叛乱。

sentences.en: Another breaks out in the next door province.
sentences.zh: 邻近省份又爆发了另一场。

sentences.en: And at one point, he says to Plowden,
sentences.zh: 有一次，他对普劳登说，

sentences.en: I have deceived myself.
sentences.zh: 我欺骗了自己。

sentences.en: This is a stiff-necked people, and it is necessary to chastise them before they enjoy the blessings which providence has intended.
sentences.zh: 这是一个顽固的民族，必须在他们享受天意注定的福祉之前惩戒他们。

sentences.en: He speaks always in this very kind of rolling biblical cadences.
sentences.zh: 他说话总是带着这种连绵起伏的圣经基调。

sentences.en: And then in 1858, a key moment, I think, his wife, who was always a moderating influence on him, it was called Tewabak.
sentences.zh: 然后在1858年，我认为是一个关键时刻，他的妻子——她对他一直有着温和的约束作用，名叫特瓦巴克。

sentences.en: She died in her late 20s, and he was absolutely bereft.
sentences.zh: 她在二十多岁时去世了，他感到无比悲痛。

sentences.en: He married again for political reasons.
sentences.zh: 出于政治原因，他再次结婚了。

sentences.en: He married a woman called Tiranesh.
sentences.zh: 他娶了一个叫蒂拉内什的女人。

sentences.en: I say a woman.
sentences.zh: 我说是个女人。

sentences.en: She was 12.
sentences.zh: 她当时才12岁。

sentences.en: And they didn't really get on.
sentences.zh: 他们其实合不来。

sentences.en: Whenever Teodros went to her tent, he would find her reading the PsalMs.
sentences.zh: 每当特奥德罗斯去她的帐篷时，他都会发现她在读《诗篇》。

sentences.en: And she would just say to him very coldly and curtly,
sentences.zh: 而她只会冷冰冰、生硬地对他说，

sentences.en: I'm conversing with a greater king than you.
sentences.zh: 我在与一位比你更伟大的君王对话。

sentences.en: Get out.
sentences.zh: 出去。

sentences.en: He clearly finds this distressing because he starts drinking very heavily at around this point.
sentences.zh: 他显然觉得这很痛苦，因为大约在这个时候他开始酗酒。

sentences.en: He starts sleeping with random women in the camp.
sentences.zh: 他开始与营地里的随机女性发生性关系。

sentences.en: And he confesses to visiting European missionaries.
sentences.zh: 他坦白自己曾去拜访欧洲传教士。

sentences.en: He says, I'm leading a very unchristian and disreputable life.
sentences.zh: 他说，我过着一种非常不基督化且声誉扫地的生活。

sentences.en: And he feels bad about it.
sentences.zh: 对此他感到很内疚。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这样。

sentences.en: Now, the second key moment is in 1860, two years later.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二个关键时刻是在1860年，也就是两年后。

sentences.en: Plowden, his friend, is traveling across Abyssinia when his party is ambushed by rebels.
sentences.zh: 普劳登，他的朋友，在穿过阿比西尼亚时，其一行人遭到叛军伏击。

sentences.en: Plowden is wounded with a spear, and he dies nine days later.
sentences.zh: 普劳登被长矛刺伤，九天后去世了。

sentences.en: So that's the end of him.
sentences.zh: 所以他的一生就此结束了。

sentences.en: He had an exciting time, but it ended prematurely.
sentences.zh: 他度过了一段精彩的时光，但结束得太早了。

sentences.en: But I guess it's the way he would have wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 但我想这正是他所期望的归宿吧。

sentences.en: It is exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely, it is.
sentences.zh: 一点没错，就是这样。

sentences.en: So the British now need to appoint a new representative on the Red Sea coaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人现在需要在红海海岸任命一位新的代表。

sentences.en: Again, it's not a priority for them.
sentences.zh: 同样，这对他们来说并不是优先事项。

sentences.en: So it takes them two years to finally send somebody out.
sentences.zh: 因此他们花了两年时间才终于派人过去。

sentences.en: And during that time, Teodros' mental state declines from bad to worse.
sentences.zh: 在那期间，特奥德罗斯的精神状况急转直下。

sentences.en: So missionaries who are writing back say he's increasingly vengeful and angry.
sentences.zh: 写信回来的传教士说他变得越来越复仇心切和愤怒。

sentences.en: He's like a man on the verge of a titanic explosion.
sentences.zh: 他就像一个处于惊天大爆炸边缘的人。

sentences.en: And part of this is obviously, you know, contextual.
sentences.zh: 这部分原因显然与当时的背景有关。

sentences.en: Abyssinia is a very violent place.
sentences.zh: 阿比西尼亚是一个非常暴力的敌方。

sentences.en: There are constant uprisings.
sentences.zh: 那里不断发生起义。

sentences.en: There's also, I think, a slight degree of paranoia.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这也带有一点妄想症的成分。

sentences.en: He's terrified that the British are conspiring, as we said, with the Ottomans and with the
sentences.zh: 他非常害怕英国人正如我们所说的那样，在与奥斯曼人和

sentences.en: Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 埃及人勾结。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with the idea that people in his entourage are plotting against him.
sentences.zh: 他执着于认为自己身边的人都在密谋反对他。

sentences.en: So he will regularly hold purges of his senior officers, and he would cut off their hands and feet, or sometimes just one hand and one foot, and then he'd throw them outside to
sentences.zh: 因此他会定期清洗高级军官，砍掉他们的手脚，或者有时只砍掉一只手和一只脚，然后把他们扔到外面

sentences.en: be devoured by hyenas.
sentences.zh: 去被鬣狗吞食。

sentences.en: That's a horrible fate.
sentences.zh: 那真是个可怕的结局。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这样。

sentences.en: We already encountered him saying to Plowden, you know, the people of Abyssinia are rather letting me down.
sentences.zh: 我们之前就遇到过他对普劳登说，你知道的，阿比西尼亚的人民实在让我失望。

sentences.en: And he really comes to believe this.
sentences.zh: 而他真的开始相信这一点了。

sentences.en: When he goes into rebel provinces, he's increasingly merciless.
sentences.zh: 当他进入叛军省份时，他越来越毫不留情。

sentences.en: He calls himself the flail of the wicked.
sentences.zh: 他称自己为恶人的皮鞭。

sentences.en: And he likes to quote one of the psalms, the righteous shall rejoice when he seeth the vengeance.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢引用《诗篇》中的一句：义人见仇敌遭报，就欢喜。

sentences.en: He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
sentences.zh: 他要在恶人的血中洗脚。

sentences.en: Washing his feet in the blood of the wicked is very much what Theodras is about by the
sentences.zh: 在恶人的血中洗脚，正是特奥德罗斯在19世纪
60年代的写照。

sentences.en: And in order to do this, he's become particularly obsessed with guns.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他变得对枪支格外痴迷。

sentences.en: No one in history, not even the people who go to your brother and Al Murray's festival, their World War II festival.
sentences.zh: 历史上没有人，甚至连去你兄弟和阿尔·穆雷的节日、他们的二战节日的人。

sentences.en: Not even those people are as interested in artillery as this guy.
sentences.zh: 甚至连那些人对火炮的热情也没有这家伙高。

sentences.en: He loves guns.
sentences.zh: 他太爱枪了。

sentences.en: He has turned to a group of Swiss and German missionaries who had settled in a place called
sentences.zh: 他向一群瑞士和德国传教士求助，他们在阿比西尼亚北部的

sentences.en: Gefat in northern Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 格法特定居了下来。

sentences.en: And he had allowed these missionaries in because they had presented themselves as craftsmen.
sentences.zh: 他之所以允许这些传教士进来，是因为他们把自己包装成工匠。

sentences.en: They said, oh, we'd like to teach, you know, interesting transferable skills to the Abyssinian people.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，我们想把有趣且可转移的技能教给阿比西尼亚人民。

sentences.en: And they'd built huts and a water wheel and a school and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们建造了小屋、水车、学校以及所有诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, that's missionary kind of activity, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是传教士的常规活动，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Missionaries are always building water wheels.
sentences.zh: 传教士总是喜欢建水车。

sentences.en: They love that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们最喜欢这种东西了。

sentences.en: But building artillery is less of a missionary activity, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 但我猜，制造火炮就不太算是传教士的业务了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: He loves this one bloke who's Swiss called Theophilus Waldmeier, who apparently is very good at mending muskets, very good with his hands.
sentences.zh: 他特别喜欢一个叫特奥菲卢斯·瓦尔德迈尔的瑞士小伙子，据说他非常擅长修补滑膛枪，心灵手巧。
zh_words: 特奥菲卢斯·瓦尔德迈尔

sentences.en: And he's always on to this guy, Waldmeier.
sentences.zh: 他总是缠着这个叫瓦尔德迈尔的家伙。

sentences.en: Can you not build me a massive cannon?
sentences.zh: 你难道不能给我造门大炮吗？

sentences.en: And over time, he says to these sort of German-speaking Swiss missionaries, could you please build me bigger and bigger guns?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他对这些说德语的瑞士传教士说，你们能不能给我造越来越大的枪？

sentences.en: And he gets them to build blast furnaces and things.
sentences.zh: 他还让他们建造高炉之类的东西。

sentences.en: This is the conditions of them staying in his country.
sentences.zh: 这是他们留在他的国家的条件。

sentences.en: And the blast furnaces keep exploding or – because actually, ultimately, they're not gunsmiths.
sentences.zh: 而高炉却不断爆炸——因为实际上，归根结底，他们并不是枪械匠。

sentences.en: They're missionaries.
sentences.zh: 他们是传教士。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: It's a big ask if you've never done it before.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前从没干过，这可是一个大难题。

sentences.en: Theodoros is very impatient.
sentences.zh: 特奥德罗斯非常急躁。

sentences.en: And he says to them, I want you to build me bigger guns.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，我要你们给我造更大的枪。

sentences.en: And I quote, if you say you don't know how, I shall regard you as liars, and you know what I do with those who deceive me.
sentences.zh: 我引述他的话：如果你说你不会，我就视你为骗子，而你知道我如何对待那些欺骗我的人。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: So that is ominous for these men of God.
sentences.zh: 所以这对这些上帝的仆人来说是个不祥之兆。

sentences.en: And it's against this background that the British finally appoint their new envoy.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种背景下，英国人终于任命了他们的新使节。

sentences.en: And he is a man called Captain Charles Duncan Cameron.
sentences.zh: 他是一个名叫查尔斯·邓肯·卡梅伦上尉的人。

sentences.en: And he rides into Theodoros' camp in October 1862.
sentences.zh: 他在1862年10月骑马进入了特奥德罗斯的军营。

sentences.en: And Cameron is a career soldier.
sentences.zh: 卡梅伦是一名职业军人。

sentences.en: He had served in South Africa and, indeed, in the Crimea before coming to Massawa on the
sentences.zh: 他在南非服过役，在来到红海海岸的马萨瓦

sentences.en: Red Sea coaSt.
sentences.zh: 之前，甚至还在克里米亚服过役。

sentences.en: And when he arrives, he has a present for Theodoros.
sentences.zh: 他抵达时，带给特奥德罗斯一件礼物。

sentences.en: It's two dueling pistols with a silver inscription.
sentences.zh: 那是两把刻有银质铭文的决斗手枪。

sentences.en: Presented to Theodore, Emperor of Abyssinia, by Victoria, Queen of Great Britain and Ireland, for his kindness to her servant, Plowden.
sentences.zh: 大不列颠及爱尔兰女王维多利亚赠予阿比西尼亚皇帝西奥多，以表彰他对她的仆人普劳登的仁慈。

sentences.en: Now, these pistols are important.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些手枪很重要。

sentences.en: We will come back to them later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会回过头来谈它们。

sentences.en: They will have an ironic function.
sentences.zh: 它们将发挥一种具有讽刺意味的作用。

sentences.en: It's great to have some dueling pistols back on the show after Alexander Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 能在亚历山大·汉密尔顿之后在节目中再次看到决斗手枪真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Cameron, he's the new guy, career soldier.
sentences.zh: 所以卡梅隆，他是新来的，职业军人。

sentences.en: He is not as pro-Abyssinia as Plowden.
sentences.zh: 他对阿比西尼亚不像普洛登那么支持。

sentences.en: He's sort of stiff.
sentences.zh: 他有点古板。

sentences.en: He's a bit inflexible.
sentences.zh: 他有点不知变通。

sentences.en: He's shocked by Theodoros' bloodthirstiness.
sentences.zh: 他对特沃德罗斯的嗜血感到震惊。

sentences.en: When Theodoros goes into his rants about launching a holy war against the Egyptians, this guy, Captain Cameron, just sort of frowns and looks a bit pained because he knows this
sentences.zh: 当特沃德罗斯长篇大论地扬言要对埃及人发动圣战时，这家伙，卡梅隆上尉，只会皱起眉头，露出痛苦的表情，因为他知道这

sentences.en: is bonkers.
sentences.zh: 太荒唐了。

sentences.en: Had Plowden kind of said, yeah, that's great, your majesty.
sentences.zh: 而普洛登以前可能会说，好的，太棒了，陛下。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Plowden had been like planning the pageantry or something.
sentences.zh: 普洛登之前一直在筹划庆典或类似的事情。

sentences.en: With apt biblical quotes.
sentences.zh: 配上恰当的圣经引文。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so now we get to a key moment in the story.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了故事中的一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: Towards the end of 1862, Cameron leaves the camp to go back to the Red Sea coaSt.
sentences.zh: 在1862年底左右，卡梅隆离开营地，返回红海海岸。

sentences.en: And Theodoros gives him a letter.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯给了他一封信。

sentences.en: And the letter reads as follows.
sentences.zh: 信的内容如下。

sentences.en: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, one God in Trinity, chosen by God, King of Kings, Theodoros of Ethiopia, to Her Majesty, Victoria, Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 奉圣父、圣子、圣灵之名，三位一体的上帝，承蒙上帝拣选、万王之王、埃塞俄比亚的特沃德罗斯，致英格兰女王维多利亚陛下。

sentences.en: Mr. Plowden used to tell me that there was a great Christian queen who loves all Christians.
sentences.zh: 普洛登先生过去常常告诉我，有一位伟大的基督教女王，她热爱所有的基督徒。

sentences.en: I was prevented by the Turks occupying the seacoast from sending you an embassy when I was in difficulty.
sentences.zh: 当我处于困境时，由于土耳其人占领了海岸，我无法向您派遣使团。

sentences.en: Consul Cameron arrived with the letter and presence of friendship.
sentences.zh: 卡梅隆领事带着信件和友好的情谊抵达了。

sentences.en: By the power of God, I was very glad.
sentences.zh: 靠着上帝的大能，我非常高兴。

sentences.en: I have received your presence and I thank you much.
sentences.zh: 我已经收到了您的心意，非常感谢您。

sentences.en: Now, I wish that you may arrange for the safe passage of my ambassadors everywhere on the road.
sentences.zh: 现在，我希望您能为我的使者在沿途各地的安全通行做出安排。

sentences.en: I wish to have an answer to this letter by Consul Cameron and that he may conduct my embassy to England.
sentences.zh: 我希望通过卡梅隆领事得到这封信的回复，并希望他能护送我的使团前往英国。

sentences.en: See how Islam oppresses the Christians.
sentences.zh: 看看伊斯兰教是如何压迫基督徒的。

sentences.en: This is the letter.
sentences.zh: 这就是这封信。

sentences.en: Cameron goes off with the letter and weeks go by and then months go by and Cameron finally returns in June 1863.
sentences.zh: 卡梅隆带着信出发了，几个星期过去了，几个月过去了，卡梅隆终于在1863年6月回来了。

sentences.en: So this is about six months later.
sentences.zh: 所以这大约是六个月后。

sentences.en: And Theodoros says, has your mistress, the Queen of England, gosh, has she written me a reply?
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯说，你的主子，英格兰女王，天哪，她给我回信了吗？

sentences.en: And Cameron says, unfortunately, I've heard nothing.
sentences.zh: 卡梅隆说，不幸的是，我没有听到任何消息。

sentences.en: I've had nothing from London.
sentences.zh: 我没有收到来自伦敦的任何消息。

sentences.en: But your majesty, I will give my head if after two months the answer to your letter is not here.
sentences.zh: 但是陛下，如果两个月后对您信件的回复还没送到这里，我愿割下我的头颅。

sentences.en: And then Cameron vanishes again.
sentences.zh: 然后卡梅隆又消失了。

sentences.en: And Theodoros hears rumours that Cameron has gone back to the coast and he's actually in
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯听到传言说卡梅隆已经回到了海岸，而且他实际上在

sentences.en: Sudanese territory.
sentences.zh: 苏丹领土上。

sentences.en: He's talking to the Sudanese.
sentences.zh: 他在跟苏丹人交谈。

sentences.en: Now, he is because the foreign office have been asking him to investigate the local slave trade, which they're keen to stamp out.
sentences.zh: 现在，他确实在这么做，因为外交部一直要求他调查当地他们热切想要根除的奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: But Theodoros thinks this bloke, he didn't seem very comfortable anyway.
sentences.zh: 但特沃德罗斯觉得这家伙，他本来就显得不太自在。

sentences.en: He was always shifty.
sentences.zh: 他总是鬼鬼祟祟的。

sentences.en: He hasn't brought me the answer to the letter.
sentences.zh: 他没有给我带来信件的回复。

sentences.en: I wonder if he's gone out there to sell me out to the MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 我在想他是不是去那里把我出卖给穆斯林了。

sentences.en: I knew the British would sell me out.
sentences.zh: 我就知道英国人会出卖我。

sentences.en: This is what he's thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的想法。

sentences.en: So more months go by and all the time Theodoros' paranoia is building.
sentences.zh: 于是更多的月份过去了，特沃德罗斯的偏执狂也与日俱增。

sentences.en: He cannot understand why Queen Victoria has not replied to his letter.
sentences.zh: 他无法理解为什么维多利亚女王没有回复他的信。

sentences.en: At best, it shows she doesn't care about him.
sentences.zh: 往最好里想，这表明她不在乎他。

sentences.en: At worst, it's a sign that she is actually plotting with his Muslim enemies.
sentences.zh: 往最坏里想，这表明她实际上在和他的穆斯林敌人密谋。

sentences.en: And then in October, his impatience and distrust finally boil over and he completely loses it.
sentences.zh: 然后到了10月，他的不耐烦和不信任终于爆发了，他彻底失控了。

sentences.en: And the man who provokes him is a missionary called Henry Aaron Stern, who was German-born in Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 激怒他的人是一个名叫亨利·亚伦·斯特恩的传教士，他出生于德国汉堡。

sentences.en: And he'd been sent to Abyssinia by a group called the London Society of Promoting Christianity
sentences.zh: 他被一个名为“伦敦促进犹太人基督教信仰协会”的组织派往阿比西尼亚

sentences.en: Among the Jews.
sentences.zh: 犹太人。

sentences.en: So they specialized in sending people to the Holy Land, to Ottoman-occupied Palestine, to try to convert people.
sentences.zh: 所以他们专门派遣人员前往圣地，前往奥斯曼帝国占领的巴勒斯坦，试图让人改宗。

sentences.en: And they started sending people to Abyssinia as well.
sentences.zh: 他们也开始向阿比西尼亚派遣人员。

sentences.en: And Stern has been in Abyssinia since 1860, and he absolutely hated it.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩自1860年以来一直在阿比西尼亚，他极其讨厌这个地方。

sentences.en: He's published a book called Wanderings Among the Falashers, which is very caustic about
sentences.zh: 他出版了一本书，名叫《法拉沙人游记》，其中对

sentences.en: Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: He said of the people of Abyssinia, they were a false, treacherous, and insolent race, absurdly
sentences.zh: 他这样评价阿比西尼亚人民：他们是一个虚伪、背信弃义且傲慢的种族，其宗教信仰极其

sentences.en: superstitious in their religious belief, and revoltingly obscene in their domestic relations.
sentences.zh: 迷信，其家庭关系极其淫秽恶劣。

sentences.en: Can I ask, has he got an Abyssinian publishing deal?
sentences.zh: 请问，他是在阿比西尼亚签了出版合同吗？

sentences.en: Presumably, this hasn't been translated into...
sentences.zh: 想必这并没有被翻译成……

sentences.en: I don't think it's been translated, but somehow, news of it has reached to your truSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有被翻译，但不知怎么的，消息传到了你的信中。

sentences.en: This guy hates you, hates your people, and has written disobliging things about you in the British press.
sentences.zh: 这家伙恨你，恨你的人民，并在英国媒体上写了对你不敬的话。

sentences.en: Anyway, Stern doesn't like Abyssinia.
sentences.zh: 总之，斯特恩不喜欢阿比西尼亚。

sentences.en: He's planning to go home.
sentences.zh: 他正计划回家。

sentences.en: And he's on his way home, when by an unbelievably unfortunate coincidence, he basically runs into Teodros' army.
sentences.zh: 正当他在回家的路上时，由于难以置信的不幸巧合，他基本上撞上了特沃德罗斯的军队。

sentences.en: And some of them have been drinking.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有些人喝了酒。

sentences.en: There's an altercation with him.
sentences.zh: 双方发生了争执。

sentences.en: And Stern ends up being arrested and beaten up, and he's dragged to Teodros' tent.
sentences.zh: 结果斯特恩被捕并遭到殴打，他被拖到了特沃德罗斯的帐篷里。

sentences.en: And then he's thrown into a tent and manacled by his hands and his feet.
sentences.zh: 然后他被扔进帐篷，手脚都被戴上了手铐脚镣。

sentences.en: And he lies there for weeks.
sentences.zh: 他在那里躺了几个星期。

sentences.en: And he's convinced that he is going to be killed.
sentences.zh: 他坚信自己死定了。

sentences.en: And basically, the only thing that keeps him going is his Christian faith.
sentences.zh: 基本上，支撑他坚持下去的唯一动力就是他的基督教信仰。

sentences.en: And then five weeks later, Stern is dragged into this huge assembly of Teodros' troops.
sentences.zh: 五周后，斯特恩被拖到特沃德罗斯庞大的军队集会现场。

sentences.en: And the emperor is sitting there on his throne.
sentences.zh: 皇帝正坐在他的宝座上。

sentences.en: And before the emperor's throne is Stern's closest colleague, who's another missionary called Henry Rosenthal.
sentences.zh: 在皇帝宝座前的是斯特恩最亲密的同事，另一位名叫亨利·罗森塔尔的传教士。

sentences.en: And he is also in chains.
sentences.zh: 他也戴着锁链。

sentences.en: And Stern thinks, oh no.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩心想，糟了。

sentences.en: And a scribe reads out the charges against them.
sentences.zh: 一名书记官宣读了对他们的指控。

sentences.en: Stern is accused of mocking Teodros' counselors, of undermining Ethiopian Christianity, of slandering
sentences.zh: 斯特恩被指控嘲笑特沃德罗斯的谋士、破坏埃塞俄比亚基督教、诽谤

sentences.en: the emperor as a war criminal, and I quote, worst of all, ridiculing the emperor's genealogy.
sentences.zh: 皇帝为战犯，我引用原话：“最糟糕的是，嘲笑皇帝的家谱。”

sentences.en: He's definitely saying that he's descended from Solomon, is he?
sentences.zh: 他绝对是说自己是所罗门的后代，对吧？

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: Actually, there's a hilarious moment at this camp.
sentences.zh: 其实，在这个营地里有一个极其搞笑的时刻。

sentences.en: When they mention the genealogy thing, Teodros says to this guy, Stern, you doubt that I'm descended from Solomon.
sentences.zh: 当他们提到家谱这事时，特沃德罗斯对这个叫斯特恩的家伙说，你怀疑我是所罗门的后代。

sentences.en: Here are the priests.
sentences.zh: 牧师们就在这里。

sentences.en: They will recite my genealogy.
sentences.zh: 他们会背诵我的家谱。

sentences.en: And the priests start to recite the genealogy.
sentences.zh: 于是牧师们开始背诵家谱。

sentences.en: And they do quite well at firSt.
sentences.zh: 一开始他们背得挺好。

sentences.en: But apparently, when they got to about the 15th or 16th century, they started to falter and to stutter.
sentences.zh: 但显然，当背到大约15世纪或16世纪时，他们开始结巴和口吃。

sentences.en: And then they started to argue among themselves.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始互相争吵。

sentences.en: And Teodros went absolutely berserk and said, next time I tell you this, you will know.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯彻底狂怒，说道，下次我告诉你们时，你们就知道了。

sentences.en: You will know my family tree.
sentences.zh: 你们就会知道我的家谱了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so this is Stern.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，这就是斯特恩的情况。

sentences.en: And then Rosenthal was accused of having written that the country would be better off under
sentences.zh: 然后罗森塔尔被指控曾写过这个国家在埃及统治下会过得更好

sentences.en: Egyptian rule.
sentences.zh: 埃及统治。

sentences.en: And Teodros says to the two of them, you Europeans came into this country and I loved, honored and respected you, but you are liars.
sentences.zh: 特沃德罗斯对他们两人说，你们欧洲人来到这个国家，我曾爱戴、尊崇和敬重你们，但你们都是骗子。

sentences.en: And then they read the verdict.
sentences.zh: 接着他们宣读了判决结果。

sentences.en: They're sentenced to death and they're dragged back to their tents.
sentences.zh: 他们被判处死刑，并被拖回了帐篷。

sentences.en: But then nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 但随后什么也没有发生。

sentences.en: Days pass and the sentence isn't carried out.
sentences.zh: 日子一天天过去，死刑并没有执行。

sentences.en: They're sometimes dragged out of the tents and forced to watch the sort of bloody execution of Abyssinian rebels and peasants.
sentences.zh: 他们有时会被拖出帐篷，被迫观看阿比西尼亚叛军和农民那种血腥的处决。

sentences.en: But the blade never falls on them.
sentences.zh: 但屠刀从未落到他们头上。

sentences.en: And in fact, their guards say to them after a few weeks, the emperor has relented.
sentences.zh: 事实上，几周后他们的卫兵对他们说，皇帝已经心软了。

sentences.en: He's probably going to release you like he's going to forget all about it.
sentences.zh: 他可能会释放你们，就像把这事完全忘掉一样。

sentences.en: And then on the 3rd of January, 1864, they're brought before the emperor once again.
sentences.zh: 然后在1864年1月3日，他们再次被带到皇帝面前。

sentences.en: And they're dragged before Teodros' throne.
sentences.zh: 他们被拖到特沃德罗斯的宝座前。

sentences.en: And they see to their relief around the throne, the British consul, Captain Cameron, and a load of other missionaries.
sentences.zh: 令他们宽慰的是，他们看到宝座周围有英国领事卡梅隆上尉和一大批其他传教士。

sentences.en: And Stern thinks to himself, thank God for that.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩心里想，感谢上帝。

sentences.en: You know, they've come and interceded for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们来为我们求情了。

sentences.en: We are free at laSt.
sentences.zh: 我们终于自由了。

sentences.en: And then in his next thought, he notices the shackles on Cameron's legs.
sentences.zh: 接着在他的下一个念头中，他注意到了卡梅隆腿上的镣铐。

sentences.en: And one of the other missionaries looks at him and he whispers, we are all prisoners now.
sentences.zh: 其中另一位传教士看着他，低声说道，我们现在都是囚犯了。

sentences.en: And it's that's the point when Stern realizes that their nightmare and this whole bonkers story are only just beginning.
sentences.zh: 正是在那一刻，斯特恩意识到他们的噩梦以及这个荒唐的故事才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: And we will find out what happens after a break.
sentences.zh: 休息之后我们将揭晓接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: This episode is supported by Anthropic, the team behind Claude.
sentences.zh: 本集由 Claude 背后的团队 Anthropic 赞助支持。

sentences.en: Now, history's biggest leaps, many of them started as hard questions that people didn't want asked.
sentences.zh: 历史上的许多重大飞跃，其中许多都始于人们不想去回答的艰难问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a classic example of that, Tom, at the end of the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 没错，汤姆，15世纪末就有一个经典的例子。

sentences.en: And the hard question in particular was, what is out there beyond the Atlantic Ocean to the
sentences.zh: 具体来说那个艰难的问题是，在大西洋西岸之外究竟有什么

sentences.en: West?
sentences.zh: 西方？

sentences.en: And as you will know, the man who found the answer to that question was the explorer Christopher
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，找到那个问题答案的人是探险家克里斯托弗

sentences.en: Columbus.
sentences.zh: 哥伦布。

sentences.en: Great pioneering voyage of discovery.
sentences.zh: 这是一次伟大的开创性发现之旅。

sentences.en: And he is, of course, the Americas.
sentences.zh: 当然，他发现了美洲。

sentences.en: So, you know, Anthropic knows the importance of questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，Anthropic 知道问题的重要性。

sentences.en: And it's why Anthropic is founded on one hard question above all.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么 Anthropic 的创立归根结底源于一个艰难的问题。

sentences.en: How can we ensure that the AI revolution really goes well for ordinary people?
sentences.zh: 我们如何确保人工智能的革命真正为普通人带来美好的结果？

sentences.en: Anthropic asked 100,000 people.
sentences.zh: Anthropic 询问了十万人。

sentences.en: And what came back wasn't just fear.
sentences.zh: 得到的反馈不仅仅是恐惧。

sentences.en: There was hope as well.
sentences.zh: 其中也有希望。

sentences.en: People wanted to know, will cancer ever be cured?
sentences.zh: 人们想知道，癌症会被治愈吗？

sentences.en: Can kids have a better future?
sentences.zh: 孩子们能拥有更美好的未来吗？

sentences.en: It turns out that there is hope in hard questions.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，艰难的问题中蕴含着希望。

sentences.en: Ask yours at claude.ai slash rest is history.
sentences.zh: 请访问 claude.ai slash rest is history 提出你的问题。

sentences.en: And keep thinking.
sentences.zh: 并保持思考。

sentences.en: The great gang struggle between Britain and Russia.
sentences.zh: 英国与俄国之间的大博弈。

sentences.en: We assess, Prime Minister, with high confidence it was Russian.
sentences.zh: 我们评估认为，首相阁下，我们有高度的信心这是俄国人干的。

sentences.zh: 追究俄国人的责任就等同于第三次世界大战。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那家伙在虚张声势，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你究竟想不想奉陪到底？

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！
